history.change: A signal must still carry its edge on the quote showing when it fires, not only on the three-minute average.

Signals stop at minute 34, not 38: the model knows nothing of fouling and clock play. An average needs three readings of its own covering two and a half minutes, and the recorder keeps a reading every 30 seconds. Team totals are dropped: their lines were implied from the total and spread, and their price was an estimate.

No signal on a stalled score feed: when the game clock has stood for five minutes, when four points have gone up or the sportsbook total has moved four points while it stood, or when a game is first seen already standing still. Signals logged on such readings before this date are marked and left out of the headline record. A signal now waits for its gap to hold: the three-minute average must stay two deviations out for a further two minutes, and the signal is logged at the line and price showing then. On the slates recorded through November 24, signals that had held two minutes won 22 of 31, and the others were close to break-even. The rule was installed at about 8 PM Central on November 24, during that slate, and no further signal was logged for it.
